He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati Bearcats]]. ==High school career== Scott played basketball for [[McIntosh County Academy]] in [[Darien, Georgia]].{{cite web|first=Justin|last=Williams|title=Theory of Relativity: Trevon Scott, UC basketball and the ties that bind|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/851607/2019/03/06/theory-of-relativity-trevon-scott-uc-basketball-and-the-ties-that-bind/|url-access=subscription|work=[[The Athletic]]|date=March 6, 2019|access-date=October 23, 2020}} His mother did not allow him to play sports unless he received at least a C grade on his [[report card|progress report]].{{cite web|first=Justin|last=Williams|title=Trevon Scott made history at UC this spring, now he's ready for what comes next|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2008999/2020/08/21/trevon-scott-made-history-at-uc-this-spring-now-hes-ready-for-what-comes-next/|url-access=subscription|work=[[The Athletic]]|date=August 21, 2020|access-date=October 23, 2020}} As a senior, he averaged 21.6 points, 14.1 rebounds, 6.5 assists and 3.5 blocks per game, earning Georgia Region 2A Player of the Year honors for his second straight season. Scott left as his school's all-time leading scorer, with 1,824 career points.{{cite web|title=Tre Scott|url=https://gobearcats.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/tre-scott/9089|work=University of Cincinnati Athletics|access-date=October 23, 2020}} A three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]] over offers from [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]] and [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]], among others.{{cite web|first=Bret|last=Favachio|title= Bearcats Recruiting: Tre Scott commits to Cincinnati|url=https://www.downthedrive.com/2014/9/15/6154129/bearcats-recruiting-tre-scott-commits-to-cincinnati|website=DownTheDrive.com|date=September 15, 2014|access-date=October 23, 2020}} ==College career== Scott [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his first year with Cincinnati. He was a [[Substitution (sport)|reserve]] in his first two seasons, averaging 3.1 points and 3.6 rebounds as a sophomore while shooting 55.4 percent. Scott moved into a starting role as a junior with the departure of [[Gary Clark (basketball)|Gary Clark]].{{cite web|first1=J. T.|last1=Smith|title=More minutes, more expectations for Tre Scott|url=https://thefrontofficenews.com/v2/2018/10/31/more-minutes-more-expectations-for-tre-scott/|website=TheFrontOfficeNews.com|date=October 31, 2018|access-date=October 23, 2020}}{{cite web|first1=J. T.|last1=Smith|title=Tre Scott is putting his stamp on the Bearcats program|url=http://thefrontofficenews.com/v2/2020/02/27/tre-scott-is-putting-his-stamp-on-the-bearcats-program/|website=TheFrontOfficeNews.com|date=February 27, 2020|access-date=October 23, 2020}} Scott averaged 9.3 points and 6.9 rebounds per game during his junior season.{{cite web|first=Phil|last=Neuffer|title=Season in Review: Trevon Scott|url=https://www.downthedrive.com/2019/5/8/18536056/cincinnati-bearcats-basketball-season-in-review-trevon-scott|website=DownTheDrive.com|date=May 8, 2019|access-date=October 23, 2020}} On February 9, 2020, he recorded a career-high 25 points, 13 rebounds and four steals in a 72–71 overtime loss to [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]]. Four days later, he scored 25 points again, while grabbing 19 rebounds, in a 92–86 overtime win over [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]].{{cite web|title=UC's Scott earns American Athletic Conference weekly honor and a national honor|url=https://local12.com/sports/uc-bearcats/ucs-scott-earns-american-athletic-conference-weekly-honor-and-a-national-honor-cincinnati-bearcats-college-basketball-trevon|work=[[WKRC (AM)]]|date=February 17, 2020|access-date=October 23, 2020}}{{cite web|title=Cincinnati rallies, beats Memphis 92-86 in overtime|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169579|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=February 13, 2020|access-date=October 23, 2020}} On February 19, Scott posted 22 points and a career-high 21 rebounds in an 89–87 double-overtime loss to [[UCF Knights men's basketball|UCF]]. He became the first Cincinnati player to register a 20-point, 20-rebound game since [[Kenyon Martin]] in 1998.{{cite web|first=Fletcher|last=Page|title=UC's Trevon Scott: End of college career 'will haunt me for the rest of my life'|url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/university-of-cincinnati/2020/04/01/trevon-scott-end-uc-career-will-haunt-me-rest-my-life/5101973002/|work=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]]|date=April 1, 2020|access-date=October 23, 2020}} As a senior, Scott averaged 11.4 points, 10.5 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 1.5 steals per game, collecting First Team All-[[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC), Defensive Player of the Year and Most Improved Player honors.{{cite web|title=UC's Scott earns three individual awards from American Athletic Conference|url=https://local12.com/sports/uc-bearcats/ucs-scott-earns-three-individual-awards-from-american-athletic-conference-cincinnati-college-basketball-trevon-prescious-achiuwa-bearcats|work=[[WKRC (AM)]]|date=March 11, 2020|access-date=October 23, 2020}} He became the first Cincinnati player since the 1982–83 season to average a [[double-double]]. Because the NCAA Tournament was cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic, Scott said the end of his collegiate career "will haunt me for the rest of my life." ==Professional career== ===Leones de Ponce
